shelter_info.generic:
**For shelter and evacuation information in Pakistan:**

1. **Contact local authorities** — district administration, NDMA (051-9205037), or your provincial PDMA
2. **Listen to emergency broadcasts** — PTV, FM 101, local radio for shelter locations
3. **Check official channels** — NDMA / PDMA Twitter/Facebook, district websites

**General shelter tips:**
- Shelters are usually set up in government schools, colleges, community halls, sports complexes
- Bring your emergency kit, medications, CNIC and important documents
- Register at the shelter for tracking purposes
- Pakistan Army / Rangers / FC often coordinate shelter operations during major disasters

Would you like the helpline number for your province?
shelter_info.prompt_location: To provide specific shelter information, I'll need to know your city or province. In the meantime, please contact your nearest district disaster management cell or call **1122**.

evacuation_route.generic:
**Evacuation Guidance:**

1. **Don't wait for an official order** if you see imminent danger (rising water, fire, collapse risk)
2. **Take only essentials** — CNIC, phone + charger, cash, medications, water, sturdy shoes
3. **Move to higher ground** for floods; **away from buildings** for earthquakes; **upwind** of fires/gas leaks
4. **Use main roads** if you can — avoid narrow streets, underpasses, bridges over flooded rivers
5. **Stay together** as a family group; assign one person to keep emergency contacts handy
6. **Tell someone outside the area** where you're going

**Don't:**
- Drive into floodwater (just 60 cm can sweep a car)
- Use elevators during fire/earthquake
- Return until authorities declare it safe

For real-time updates, follow your provincial PDMA on social media.

- **Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD)** — pmd.gov.pk
- **Flood Forecasting Division** — 042-99200296
- **NDMA** — ndma.gov.pk

**Severe-Weather Seasons in Pakistan:**
- **Monsoon:** July–September (flooding, urban inundation)
- **Heatwave:** May–June (especially Sindh, southern Punjab)
- **Winter snow / avalanches:** December–February (GB, AJK, Northern KPK)
- **Cyclone window:** May–June and Oct–Nov (coastal Sindh/Balochistan)

report_incident.default:
**To report an incident or emergency in Pakistan:**

1. **Immediate emergency:** call {emergency_number} (Rescue 1122) or **115** (Edhi)

2. **Non-emergency reports:**
   - Local police station (or **15**)
   - District disaster management cell
   - Provincial PDMA helpline
   - SafeLink in-app incident report

**When reporting, provide:**
- Your location (city, neighbourhood, landmark)
- Type of incident (fire, flood, accident, structural collapse, gas leak)
- Number of people affected (if known)
- Any immediate dangers (live wires, gas leak, blocked exit)

Would you like the helpline numbers for your province?
report_incident.acknowledged:
Thank you for reporting this. Here's what to do next:

1. If not done yet, call emergency services: {emergency_number}
2. Stay safe and keep distance from danger
3. Help others evacuate if it's safe to do so
4. Follow instructions from emergency responders

donation_volunteering.generic:
**Trusted disaster-relief organisations in Pakistan:**

- **Edhi Foundation** — edhi.org / 115 / Bank Al Habib & HBL accounts on website
- **Chhipa Welfare** — chhipa.org / 1020
- **JDC Foundation** — jdcwelfare.org / 0311-1112400
- **Saylani Welfare** — saylaniwelfare.com
- **Pakistan Red Crescent** — prcs.org.pk / 051-9250404
- **Al-Khidmat Foundation** — alkhidmat.org
- **Akhuwat** — akhuwat.org.pk (interest-free loans for victims)
- **Shaukat Khanum** — shaukatkhanum.org.pk (medical aid)
- **NDMA Citizen Donation** — ndma.gov.pk

**To volunteer:**
- Register with one of the above organisations during active relief operations
- Pakistan Red Crescent and Edhi run regular volunteer training
- Don't go independently to a disaster zone without coordination — it can hinder relief efforts

**To donate effectively:**
- Money is more useful than goods (organisations buy locally)
- Avoid sending random clothes/food to disaster sites unless requested
- Verify the organisation before donating online

mental_health.generic:
**Mental health support after a disaster — it's normal to feel overwhelmed.**

Common reactions: anxiety, sleeplessness, intrusive thoughts, irritability, sadness, guilt. Most people recover with time, support, and self-care. Reach out if symptoms persist beyond a few weeks or worsen.

**Free counseling lines in Pakistan:**
- **Rozan Counseling Helpline** — 0304-1111741 (depression, trauma)
- **Umang Helpline** — 0311-7786264 (youth-focused)
- **Taskeen** — taskeen.org (online resources)

**Self-care basics:**
- Talk to family or trusted friends
- Keep a routine — regular meals, sleep
- Limit news/social media exposure
- Light exercise / walking helps
- Religious or community practices, if they help you

**Seek professional help if:**
- Thoughts of self-harm or suicide → call **115** immediately
- Inability to function for more than 2 weeks
- Severe panic, flashbacks, or numbness

quick_tips.earthquake:
🏠 **Quick Earthquake Tips (Pakistan):**
DROP, COVER, HOLD ON | Stay away from windows | Don't run outside during shaking | Call **1122** or **115** | Expect aftershocks
quick_tips.flood:
🌊 **Quick Flood Tips (Pakistan):**
Move to higher ground | Never walk/drive through flood water (60 cm sweeps a car) | Call **1122** or **115** | NDMA: **051-9205037** | Watch for snakes & live wires after water recedes
quick_tips.heatwave:
🌡️ **Quick Heatwave Tips:**
Stay indoors 11 AM–4 PM | Drink water every 15 min, even if not thirsty | ORS for outdoor workers | Cool with wet cloth on neck/wrists | Heat stroke = call **115** immediately
quick_tips.fire:
🔥 **Quick Fire Tips:**
GET OUT, STAY OUT | Crawl under smoke (cleaner air below) | Stop, Drop, Roll if clothes catch fire | Never use elevator | Call **16** (Fire) or **1122**
quick_tips.cyclone:
🌀 **Quick Cyclone Tips (Coastal Sindh/Balochistan):**
Follow PMD / PDMA evacuation orders | Move inland & upward | Stay indoors away from windows | Don't go out during the calm 'eye' of storm | Call **1122**
quick_tips.tsunami:
🌊 **Quick Tsunami Tips (Coastal areas):**
If you feel a strong earthquake near the coast → move to high ground IMMEDIATELY | Don't wait for official warning | Stay there until authorities all-clear
quick_tips.snake_bite:
🐍 **Quick Snake-Bite Tips:**
Keep the person still & calm | Remove rings/watches before swelling | Don't cut, suck, or apply tourniquet | Note snake colour/length if safe | Rush to nearest hospital — anti-venom needed | Call **1122**
quick_tips.gas_leak:
⛽ **Quick Gas-Leak Tips:**
DO NOT switch on/off any electrical | Don't light matches | Open windows & doors | Evacuate everyone | Call **1199** (SSGC/SNGPL) from a safe distance
quick_tips.building_collapse:
🏚️ **Quick Building-Collapse Tips:**
If trapped: stay calm, cover mouth/nose, tap on pipes/walls (don't shout — saves oxygen) | Outside: don't enter — wait for Rescue 1122 | Note exact location of trapped people for responders
quick_tips.electric_shock:
⚡ **Quick Electric-Shock Tips:**
NEVER touch the person while connected to power | Switch off main breaker first | Use a dry wooden stick to push the source away | Once safe → check breathing, start CPR if needed | Call **115**
quick_tips.pandemic:
😷 **Quick Pandemic Tips:**
Wash hands frequently | Wear masks in crowds | Maintain distance | Get vaccinated | Follow official health advisories from NIH Pakistan
